problems.description: The commit deletes the entire seed codebase (index.ts, the tier-1 Express Todo API) and replaces it with an unrelated static-site-generator project. No seams, models, or structure were carried over, so the multi-session story loses its baseline rather than evolving it.

Convention score 0.53 with 31 violations, all clustered in cli.ts, config.ts, and generator.ts: non-PascalCase classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants, and snake_case functions — the new modules do not follow the naming conventions the rest of the repo enforces.

Two divergent entry points: bin/ssg.js imports the compiled lib/cli.js while the package.json 'start' script runs tsx src/cli.ts, and 'main' points to lib/generator.js — so the CLI breaks unless a build step runs first, with no explicit build hook on install.
Direct-execution detection in cli.ts relies on a fragile regex test of process.argv[1] (/cli\.(?:js|ts)$/), duplicating the guard already handled by bin/ssg.js.
Two runtime deps (gray-matter, markdown-it) introduced wholesale for session 1; reasonable for an SSG, but nothing reused from the seed's dependency set, widening the surface.

strengths: Clean separation of concerns: bin/cli/generator/config layering keeps I/O, parsing, and rendering decoupled.
Robust file handling via async fs/promises and recursive directory traversal that respects nested content dirs.
Slugs derived from filesystem-relative paths and stable title-based sorting give deterministic output.
Metadata values are guarded and HTML-escaped before rendering, avoiding raw injection into generated pages.
commit_reviews.summary: A functionally clean greenfield SSG structure, but it wholesale-replaces the seed baseline, ignores repo naming conventions (0.53, 31 violations), and introduces a compiled-lib/tsx entry-point mismatch, so net-net it is worse than the baseline it removed.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity jumps +19 concentrated in createRenderer/render: a nested closure with a triple-fallback resolution chain (`templates.get(requested) ?? (name ? undefined : templates.get(default)) ?? fallback`) is hard to read and reason about.

Page.data stores the raw frontmatter object and renderPage spreads `{ ...page.data, ...page }`, duplicating fields already extracted individually (title/date/tags/template/layout). The redundant `data` field invites field-collision confusion between raw and normalized values.

New module-level constants defaultPageTemplate and defaultLayoutTemplate are lowerCamelCase; mechanical convention score is 0.53 and constants-are-UPPER_CASE is among the flagged violations (also functions-should-not-be-snake_case and PascalCase rules).

Two rendering paradigms now coexist: pages go through Handlebars templates while renderIndex still uses inline string interpolation, so the output shell for index.html and page.html are generated differently.
handlebars.compile is invoked on every page render inside the render closure instead of being compiled once in createRenderer; no template compilation cache.

strengths: Templates/layouts are a canonical SSG feature; the addition slots cleanly into the existing readPages -> buildSite -> writeFile pipeline and reuses the same options/config pattern as content/output.
Replaces hand-rolled HTML-string interpolation with a real template abstraction and a focused single dependency (handlebars ^4.7.8); SonarQube smells drop -1 with +0 bugs and +0 duplications.
Tests updated in the same commit (tests/generator.test.ts) alongside the feature.
Handlebars' default escaping preserves XSS safety for interpolated title/date/tags, and `{{{html}}}` correctly treats the markdown body as trusted markup.
commit_reviews.summary: Well-fitted, well-tested templating feature that improves the SSG's flexibility, held back by a complexity spike in the renderer and redundant frontmatter handling.

problems.description: The entire serve subsystem (server.ts) is added with zero tests despite jest + ts-jest being configured: --port parsing/validation, the path-traversal guard, live-reload HTML injection, and the rebuild queue are all untested, which is significant for a +197-line module with cognitive complexity +52.

SonarQube delta shows +52 cognitive complexity and +3 smells concentrated in the HTTP handler, rebuild()/queueing logic, and the inline live-reload script string; extracting the reload script and the handler into smaller named pieces would reduce it.

Two new runtime dependencies (chokidar, ws) serve a development-only feature; ws is a heavyweight dep for a dev server and could arguably live under optionalDependencies, though 'serve' being a shipped command justifies dependencies.

strengths: Dev-server functionality is cleanly isolated into a new src/server.ts module rather than bloating generator.ts, and ServeOptions reuses the existing BuildOptions type.
requestedFile() defends against path traversal via resolve + prefix check against the output directory.
Rebuild deduplication via the rebuilding/rebuildQueued flag prevents overlapping builds on bursty file-watcher events.
CLI extension follows the existing parseArguments pattern exactly, with proper --port integer validation and a uniform usage string.
Uses node: prefixed builtins and type-only imports (import type FSWatcher/Server), matching the codebase's import conventions.
commit_reviews.summary: A natural, well-scoped 'serve' feature that integrates cleanly with the existing generator and CLI patterns, but it ships a substantial untested subsystem (complexity +52, no test additions) that needs coverage.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity rose +17 (net) on a refactor whose purpose is simplification; hook-dispatch indirection (runHook/runFileHooks iterating plugins with dynamic plugin[hook] calls) concentrates complexity in control flow while spreading logic across 5 new files.

loadPlugins() dynamically imports 'ssg.config.ts' at runtime via pathToFileURL; under plain Node this fails unless the toolchain pre-transpiles TS, creating a hidden runtime dependency on a TS-aware loader.
Four-hook plugin system plus config file for only two built-in plugins (markdown, template) is likely premature abstraction — +5 files and +28 imports for a seam the project may never exercise.

Mechanical convention score 0.53 with 31 violations across cli.ts, config.ts, generator.ts (Classes/Interfaces PascalCase, Constants UPPER_CASE, Functions not snake_case). NOTE: reported violations contradict the code visible in this diff (SsgConfig is PascalCase, functions are camelCase), suggesting the checker may be misfiring against the codebase's actual style; flagging per instructions since measurements are ground truth.

strengths: Cohesive plugin seam (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) cleanly separates markdown, template, and config concerns — a standard pattern for static site generators.
Large net simplification: -289 lines, zero new bugs, duplications unchanged at 0.0%, and duplicated recursive directory walkers (markdownFiles/templateFiles) removed.
Public API preserved: BuildOptions/Page/Plugin re-exported from './plugin.js', so no caller breakage.
Consistent modern ESM style (node: prefixes, .js import specifiers, typed interfaces) matching the surrounding codebase.
commit_reviews.summary: Directionally sound separation-of-concerns refactor toward a plugin architecture with a big LOC reduction, but it trades simplicity for abstraction — net cognitive complexity +17, +1 smell, and a low 0.53 convention score (with checker discrepancies) leave the codebase in a heavier, arguably worse state than before.

problems.description: buildSite's return type is silently changed from Promise<Page[]> to BuildPages = Page[] & { buildStats } fabricated via Object.assign(context.pages, { buildStats }) — an array-with-attached-properties anti-pattern that breaks the public contract and forces the CLI to reach into array-props (pages.buildStats.*); a { pages, stats } result object would be cleaner.

timeSavedMs is a fabricated pseudo-metric: (elapsedMs / pagesBuilt) * pagesSkipped; when every page is skipped (pagesBuilt=0) it reports elapsedMs × pageCount, wildly overstating savings while being presented as measured output.
CacheEntry.html stores the full rendered HTML in .ssg-cache.json but the cache-hit path never reads it back (only sourceHash/templateHash are compared), bloating the manifest with redundant content.

markdown.ts adds a module-level parsedPageCache Map that never evicts deleted/renamed files (unbounded growth, stale entries) and introduces a second cache layer with invalidation logic divergent from the manifest cache.
'Incremental' still reads and hashes every source file plus the entire template tree (hashTemplates reads all .hbs contents) on every build, so it only skips render cost, not I/O cost.

Mechanical convention score is 0.53 with 31 violations (UPPER_CASE constants, PascalCase classes, no snake_case) — but inspection shows most are pre-existing whole-file lint flags; new code is stylistically consistent aside from the camelCase constant cacheFileName and the interface types BuildPages/BuildStats introduced here.
No test asserts the timeSavedMs math (the fabricated stat is untested), though the build/skip counts are well covered.

strengths: Cache invalidation is correctly keyed on sourceHash + templateHash + output-existence, and the markdown plugin does populate sourceHash (verified in the full commit, not just the truncated diff)
Comprehensive incremental-build tests cover the full matrix: unchanged, changed source, changed template, missing cache, and clean rebuild
Feature reuses the existing hook pipeline (runHook/runFileHooks) and CLI option plumbing, and template hashing is deterministic (sorted entries)
Stale-output cleanup for removed pages and .ssg-cache.json added to .gitignore
No new bugs or duplication (SonarQube +0 bugs, 0.0% dup); only +1 smell and +26 cognitive complexity, consistent with the dense buildSite loop
commit_reviews.summary: A tested and functionally correct incremental-build feature is undermined by an array-props return-type hack, a fabricated timeSavedMs metric, and an unbounded second cache layer — making the codebase marginally worse despite good coverage and no new bugs.

compounding_issues: Seed mismatch: the 2aeb626 seed was an Express Todo API, unrelated to static_site_gen; Session 1 wholesale-replaced it (index.ts deleted, -93 lines), so no baseline seams/models were ever carried into the story (S1 review: architectural_fit 0.45, 'worse')

Session 1 convention debt (mechanical score 0.53, 31 violations) was never remediated and stayed flat at 0.53 through S4, though the checker appears to misfire against actual PascalCase/camelCase code
Entry-point mismatch from S1 (bin/ssg.js -> compiled lib/cli.js vs 'start' via tsx src/cli.ts, 'main' -> lib/generator.js) persisted unresolved, leaving the CLI broken without an explicit build step
S3 shipped a +197-line dev-server subsystem with cognitive complexity +52 and zero tests; that untested surface was carried forward through S4/S5

S4's plugin/hook abstraction (5 new files, 4 lifecycle hooks, dynamic ssg.config.ts import) was premature for 2 built-in plugins and introduced a hidden runtime dependency on a TS-aware loader for loadPlugins(); complexity rose +17 on a 'simplification' refactor
Two rendering paradigms coexisted from S2 onward: pages via Handlebars but renderIndex via inline string interpolation, never consolidated
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield rebuild: discard the mismatched seed and build a standalone Markdown->HTML SSG (frontmatter, slug-based output, index page) with gray-matter + markdown-it
Session 2 chose Handlebars over EJS, adding per-page frontmatter template/layout selection, layout wrappers, and partials with a triple-fallback render resolution chain
Session 3 integrated a dev-server 'serve' command using chokidar file watching plus WebSocket live-reload injection and a rebuild queue
Session 4 refactored rendering into a lifecycle-hook plugin architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with MarkdownPlugin/TemplatePlugin and runtime ssg.config.ts loading

Session 5 built incremental builds on the plugin seam: SHA-256 source + template hashing into .ssg-cache.json, BuildStats reporting, --incremental/--clean flags, an in-memory parsedPageCache, and a dedicated dev-server plugin
story_review.trajectory_description: The quality arc is upward but uneven. Session 1 opened poorly (fit 0.45) by discarding the unrelated seed wholesale and inheriting a 0.53 convention score plus an entry-point mismatch. Sessions 2 and 3 improved decisively (fit 0.76, then 0.85) by layering well-scoped, well-tested features — Handlebars templating then a live-reload dev server — though S3 added a large untested subsystem (complexity +52). Session 4 was a temporary regression (fit 0.6, 'worse') as an over-engineered plugin refactor shipped premature abstraction and raised complexity. Session 5 recovered and peaked, producing the most sophisticated feature (content-hashed incremental caching) that directly validated the S4 plugin architecture, with the test suite expanded to cover the caching semantics. Sonar stayed bug-free throughout (bugs delta 0) and the final code is functionally coherent, but convention adherence never improved and the untested serve surface remained.
story_review.summary: A largely coherent product arc — build, template, integrate, refactor, cross-cutting cache — that ended strong after a mid-story over-abstraction dip, hampered by a mismatched seed thrown away in Session 1, persistent convention debt, and an untested dev-server subsystem.
